IWH = Interwetten home win odds
IWD = Interwetten draw odds
IWA = Interwetten away win odds
VCH = VC Bet home win odds (now BetVictor)
VCD = VC Bet draw odds (now BetVictor)
VCA = VC Bet away win odds (now BetVictor)
Bb1X2 = Number of BetBrain bookmakers used to calculate match odds averages and maximums
BbMxH = Betbrain maximum home win odds
BbAvH = Betbrain average home win odds
BbMxD = Betbrain maximum draw odds
BbAvD = Betbrain average draw win odds
BbMxA = Betbrain maximum away win odds
BbAvA = Betbrain average away win odds
BbOU = Number of BetBrain bookmakers used to calculate over/under 2.5 goals (total goals) averages and maximums
BbMx>2.5 = Betbrain maximum over 2.5 goals
BbAv>2.5 = Betbrain average over 2.5 goals
BbMx<2.5 = Betbrain maximum under 2.5 goals
BbAv<2.5 = Betbrain average under 2.5 goals
BbAH = Number of BetBrain bookmakers used to Asian handicap averages and maximums
BbAHh = Betbrain size of handicap (home team)
BbMxAHH = Betbrain maximum Asian handicap home team odds
BbAvAHH = Betbrain average Asian handicap home team odds
BbMxAHA = Betbrain maximum Asian handicap away team odds
BbAvAHA = Betbrain average Asian handicap away team odds

Notice that all of these variables represent the odds of a match. Since these features depend on people's perception, I will not be using these in my model as I only want to train my model on match statistics.

To clean the data I will now just delete all the odds columns from all of the datasets and only keep match statistics.

```{r}
# columns to keep i.e. match information, results and match statistics
columns_to_keep <- c("Date", "HomeTeam", "AwayTeam","FTHG", "HG", "FTAG", "AG", "FTR", "Res","HTHG", "HTAG", "HTR","Attendance","HS", "AS", "HST", "AST", "HHW", "AHW","HC", "AC", "HF", "AF", "HFKC", "AFKC","HO", "AO", "HY", "AY", "HR", "AR", "HBP", "ABP","HomeMatchPoints","AwayMatchPoints","HomePointsBeforeMatch","HomePointsAfterMatch","AwayPointsBeforeMatch","AwayPointsAfterMatch")


for (i in seq_along(vectordata)) {
  columns_removed <- setdiff(names(vectordata[[i]]), columns_to_keep) #odds columns

  vectordata[[i]] <- vectordata[[i]][, intersect(columns_to_keep, names(vectordata[[i]])),drop = FALSE]

  cat(names(vectordata)[i], "- removed",length(columns_removed), "columns;",ncol(vectordata[[i]]), "columns remaining\n")
}
```
As we can see, the older (or incomplete for `data26_27`) the dataset is, the less features it contains. This will then be spoken about in the limitations section of our report. This means that we want the model to be weighted more strongly for the newer datasets.

## Test/Train split

```{r}
library(dplyr)

train_names <- paste0("data",c("14_15", "15_16", "16_17", "17_18", "18_19","19_20", "20_21", "21_22", "22_23", "23_24", "24_25"))

train_data <- bind_rows(vectordata[train_names])
test_data  <- bind_rows(vectordata["data25_26"])
```
Keep 2026/27 separate as the data we'll predict from

```{r}
prediction_data <- bind_rows(vectordata["data26_27"])
```

We need to add the following columns for our model:
- Home Team total number of goals before match = HTGB
- Home Team total number of goals after match = HTGA
- Away Team total number of goals before match = ATGB
- Away Team total number of goals after match = ATGA

```{r}

# Create the new columns
train_data$HTGB <- NA
train_data$HTGA <- NA
train_data$ATGB <- NA
train_data$ATGA <- NA

teams_train <- unique(c(train_data$HomeTeam, train_data$AwayTeam)) # vector of premier league teams (2014/15-2024/25)

for (team in teams_train) {
  # Goals scored by this team in each row
  goals_scored <- ifelse(train_data$HomeTeam == team, train_data$FTHG,train_data$FTAG) #if team is home team, return FTHG, otherwise return FTAG

  goals_before <- c(0, head(cumsum(goals_scored), -1))  #team total goals before match
  goals_after  <- cumsum(goals_scored) #team total goals after match

  # Store the totals in the appropriate home or away columns
  home_rows <- train_data$HomeTeam == team 
  away_rows <- train_data$AwayTeam == team

  train_data$HTGB[home_rows] <- goals_before[home_rows]
  train_data$HTGA[home_rows] <- goals_after[home_rows]
  train_data$ATGB[away_rows] <- goals_before[away_rows]
  train_data$ATGA[away_rows] <- goals_after[away_rows]
}
```
Now we also want to add the following columns to our model:
- Home Team total points before match = HTPB
- Home team total points after match = HTPA
- Away Team total points before match = ATPB
- Away team total points after match = ATPA

```{r}
# Create the new columns
train_data$HTPB <- NA  
train_data$HTPA <- NA  
train_data$ATPB <- NA  
train_data$ATPA <- NA 

for (team in teams_train) {
  # Find every match involving this team
  rows <- which(train_data$HomeTeam == team | train_data$AwayTeam == team)

  # Points this team earned in each match
  points <- ifelse(train_data$HomeTeam[rows] == team, #if we are looking at home team
    ifelse(train_data$FTR[rows] == "H", 3,ifelse(train_data$FTR[rows] == "D", 1, 0)), #if FTR = H then 3, o/w if FTR=D then 1, o/w 0
    ifelse(train_data$FTR[rows] == "A",#if we're looking at away team and FTR = A 
           3, #then 3
           ifelse(train_data$FTR[rows] == "D", 1, 0)) #o/w if FTR = D then 1, o/w 0
  )

  # Running total before and after each match
  points_before <- c(0, head(cumsum(points), -1))
  points_after <- cumsum(points)

  # Store totals in the home or away columns
  home_rows <- rows[train_data$HomeTeam[rows] == team]
  away_rows <- rows[train_data$AwayTeam[rows] == team]

  train_data$HTPB[home_rows] <- points_before[train_data$HomeTeam[rows] == team]
  train_data$HTPA[home_rows] <- points_after[train_data$HomeTeam[rows] == team]
  train_data$ATPB[away_rows] <- points_before[train_data$AwayTeam[rows] == team]
  train_data$ATPA[away_rows] <- points_after[train_data$AwayTeam[rows] == team]
}

```
